title: A deployed RAG system scores only the final answer, so a retrieval regression is indistinguishable from a generation regression
problem: My eval suite gives one number for the answer, so when quality drops I cannot tell whether the right chunk was never retrieved or the model had it and did not use it, and I end up tuning prompts against an index problem.
symptom: Answer-level scores move and nobody can attribute the move. There is no recall@k, no ranking metric, and no labelled query-to-document set, so every investigation starts by reading transcripts by hand, and a chunking or index change ships with no measurement of what it did to retrieval.
why_now: Retrieval evaluation needs query-to-document relevance labels that do not exist for a private corpus, and the labels have to be produced before any retrieval metric can be computed, so teams ship the end-to-end answer score, which is cheap, and defer the retrieval score, which is not. The two dominant managed stacks both now document a separate retrieval evaluator, which is evidence the split matters and that the default state of a deployed pipeline does not have it.
existing: End-to-end answer graders and LLM judges are widely deployed, but a single answer score is a sum over two stages and cannot localise which one failed.
Generic RAG metric libraries ship retrieval metrics, yet they still require a labelled evaluation set per corpus; without labels the retrieval metrics silently go unused while the answer metrics run.
Managed retrieval evaluators exist (Microsoft Foundry's document_retrieval, Databricks' retrieval metrics), which closes the tooling half and leaves the labels and the wiring as the team's problem.

evidence.title: Seven Failure Points When Engineering a Retrieval Augmented Generation System
evidence.quote: validation of a RAG system is only feasible during operation
evidence.note: Experience report from three RAG deployments (two in live use), stated as one of the paper's two key takeaways. If validation only happens in operation, no pre-deploy retrieval measurement exists to regress against.

evidence.title: Seven Failure Points When Engineering a Retrieval Augmented Generation System
evidence.quote: RAG systems are difficult to test as no data exists and needs to be experimentally discovered
evidence.note: Same deployment report, naming the missing input directly: the query-to-document labels a retrieval metric needs do not exist for a private corpus, which is why the retrieval stage goes unmeasured while answer scores get computed.

evidence.title: Seven Failure Points When Engineering a Retrieval Augmented Generation System
evidence.quote: The answer to the question is in the document but did not rank highly enough to be returned to the user.
evidence.note: Failure point FP2 from the deployed systems. This is a pure ranking failure, invisible to an answer-only score, which is the class of defect the gap is about.

evidence.title: Assess performance: Metrics that matter - Azure Databricks | Microsoft Learn
evidence.quote: A RAG application can respond poorly despite retrieving the correct context; it can also provide good responses based on faulty retrievals. Only by measuring both components can we accurately diagnose and address issues in the application.
evidence.note: A vendor stating the attribution problem in the same terms: an answer-only score cannot separate the two stages, so both must be measured.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) evaluators - Microsoft Foundry
evidence.quote: The most precise measurement is to use the document_retrieval evaluator to evaluate retrieval quality and optimize your search parameters for RAG.
evidence.note: The retrieval-only evaluator is a distinct, separately-invoked component that needs relevance labels, which is why an existing eval suite can be entirely answer-level and still look complete.

build_hypothesis: A label-bootstrapping harness for retrieval only: capture production queries plus the chunk set that was actually returned and the chunk the answer cited, treat the cited chunk as a weak positive label, and emit recall@k and a ranking metric per index build. It gives a retrieval number that moves before any human labels exist, and it fails loudly when a chunking or embedding change drops recall, which is the signal an answer-level score cannot produce.

check.manual_question: For this pipeline, what number tells you that retrieval got worse without the answer score moving, and where do its query-to-document relevance labels come from?
check.rationale: The signature is a repo that retrieves from a vector store AND already evaluates something (an eval or test surface exists), while no file anywhere names a retrieval-only metric. That combination says the team measures the answer and not the retrieval step, so a ranking or chunking regression cannot be attributed. Two ways it can be wrong: a team may compute recall under a house-specific name this pattern does not know (false PRESENT), or may merely mention a metric name in a doc without computing it per build (false mitigation), so the manual question asks which number moves and where its labels come from rather than which word appears.
